questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: At 25Â°C, a neutral aqueous solution has pH approximately:
questions.explanation: At 25Â°C neutral water has equal hydrogen and hydroxide ion concentrations and pH 7.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Isotopes of the same element have the same number of:
questions.explanation: Isotopes share atomic number but differ in neutron number.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The atomic number of an element equals the number of:
questions.explanation: Atomic number is defined by the number of protons in the nucleus.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The maximum number of electrons in a shell with principal quantum number n is:
questions.explanation: The shell capacity formula is 2n squared.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The maximum number of electrons that can occupy a shell with principal quantum number n = 3 is:
questions.explanation: The maximum shell capacity is 2nÂ²; for n = 3, 2 Ã 3Â² = 18 electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Amino acids are joined in proteins by:
questions.explanation: A peptide bond links the amino group of one amino acid to the carboxyl group of another.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A hydrogen bond is strongest when hydrogen is bonded to a highly electronegative atom such as:
questions.explanation: N, O and F create strongly polar bonds and can participate in hydrogen bonding.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: An ionic bond is primarily due to:
questions.optionA: Electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions
questions.optionB: Sharing a pair of electrons equally
questions.explanation: Ionic bonding involves attraction between cations and anions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The shape of a methane molecule, CH4, is:
questions.explanation: Four bonding pairs around carbon arrange tetrahedrally to minimize repulsion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which molecular shape is associated with an spÂ³-hybridised central atom having one lone pair and three bond pairs?
questions.explanation: Four electron domains give a tetrahedral electron-pair arrangement; one lone pair leaves a trigonal-pyramidal molecular shape, as in NHâ.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A catalyst affects chemical equilibrium by:
questions.optionA: Increasing equilibrium yield in every case
questions.explanation: A catalyst speeds forward and reverse reactions without changing equilibrium composition.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For a given reaction, the equilibrium constant at a fixed temperature changes when:
questions.optionB: The system is compressed for any reaction
questions.explanation: The equilibrium constant depends on temperature, not on catalyst or initial concentration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For an exothermic equilibrium, increasing temperature generally shifts the equilibrium toward:
questions.optionA: Products, because heat is a reactant
questions.optionC: Reactants, because heat acts as a product
questions.explanation: Heating an exothermic system adds product-like heat, so equilibrium shifts toward reactants.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For a first-order reaction, the half-life is:
questions.optionB: Inversely proportional to rate constant squared
questions.explanation: For a first-order reaction, t₁/₂ = 0.693/k, independent of initial concentration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The rate of a reaction generally increases with temperature because:
questions.optionA: A larger fraction of molecules can overcome activation energy
questions.explanation: Higher temperature increases the fraction of collisions with sufficient energy to react.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The unit of a first-order rate constant is:
questions.explanation: For a first-order reaction, rate = k[A], so k has units of inverse time.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The coordination number of cobalt in [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₃ is:
questions.explanation: Six ammonia ligands are directly coordinated to cobalt, giving coordination number six.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The ligand in a coordination complex acts as a:
questions.optionA: Lewis base donating an electron pair
questions.optionB: Lewis acid accepting an electron pair only
questions.explanation: A ligand donates a lone pair to the central metal atom or ion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: At the cathode during an electrochemical reaction, which process occurs?
questions.explanation: Reduction is gain of electrons and occurs at the cathode in both galvanic and electrolytic cells.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For a galvanic cell operating spontaneously under standard conditions, E°cell is:
questions.optionC: Equal to the anode potential alone
questions.explanation: A spontaneous galvanic cell has positive standard cell potential; ΔG° = −nFE°cell.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In a galvanic cell, reduction takes place at the:
questions.explanation: Reduction occurs at the cathode; oxidation occurs at the anode.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Oxidation occurs at the:
questions.explanation: Oxidation takes place at the anode in both galvanic and electrolytic cells.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: An alkene contains at least one:
questions.explanation: Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons containing a C=C bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon in excess oxygen produces:
questions.explanation: Complete combustion oxidises carbon to COâ and hydrogen to HâO; insufficient oxygen may produce CO or soot.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: One mole contains approximately:
questions.explanation: Avogadro's constant is approximately 6.022 Ã 10 to the power 23 per mole.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Benzene is classified as:
questions.explanation: Benzene is a cyclic conjugated aromatic hydrocarbon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The IUPAC name of CHâCHâOH is:
questions.explanation: The two-carbon alcohol CH3CH2OH is named ethanol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The functional group of a carboxylic acid is:
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids contain the carboxyl group âCOOH.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The functional group of an aldehyde is:
questions.explanation: Aldehydes contain a terminal carbonyl group written as âCHO.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which reagent is commonly used to test for a carbon-carbon double bond in an unsaturated compound?
questions.explanation: Bromine water is decolourised by many compounds containing carbon-carbon double bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A carbon atom in a typical alkene C=C bond is generally:
questions.explanation: Each alkene carbon forms three sigma-bonding regions and retains a p orbital for the pi bond, corresponding to spÂ² hybridisation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which reagent is commonly used to distinguish an aldehyde from most ketones by giving a silver mirror with aldehydes?
questions.explanation: Aldehydes generally reduce Tollens’ reagent to metallic silver; most simple ketones do not give this test.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Across a period, atomic radius generally:
questions.explanation: Increasing effective nuclear charge pulls electrons closer across a period.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Elements in the same group generally have similar chemical properties because they have similar:
questions.explanation: Similar valence electron configurations lead to similar bonding behaviour.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which element has the highest electronegativity on the Pauling scale?
questions.explanation: Fluorine is the most electronegative element on the Pauling scale.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Reduction involves:
questions.explanation: Reduction is gain of electrons and a decrease in oxidation number.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The oxidation number of oxygen in most ordinary oxides is:
questions.explanation: Oxygen is usually â2 in oxides; common exceptions include peroxides, superoxides and compounds with fluorine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A solution with 1 mole of solute in 1 litre of solution has molarity:
questions.explanation: Molarity is moles of solute per litre of total solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For a dilute solution of a non-volatile solute, relative lowering of vapour pressure is equal to the solute:
questions.explanation: Raoult’s law gives relative lowering of vapour pressure equal to the mole fraction of the non-volatile solute.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For an ideal dilute solution, Raoult's law relates partial vapour pressure to:
questions.explanation: The partial vapour pressure equals the pure-component vapour pressure times its mole fraction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What is the molarity of a solution containing 0.50 mol solute in 2.0 L of solution?
questions.explanation: Molarity = moles of solute / volume of solution in litres = 0.50 / 2.0 = 0.25 mol Lâ»Â¹.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: At constant pressure, the heat exchanged by a system equals the change in which thermodynamic quantity, when only pressure-volume work is considered?
questions.explanation: For a process at constant pressure with only pressure-volume work, qâ = ÎH.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For an exothermic reaction, the enthalpy change is usually:
questions.explanation: Heat is released by the system, so its enthalpy change is negative at constant pressure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The SI unit of entropy is:
questions.explanation: Entropy is energy per kelvin; molar entropy is commonly expressed as J molâ1 Kâ1.
